scope: The host-git-fork failure only; the fixture-retention failure from the same run stays open.

original.test: integration/host-git-fork: one actual workspace owner fences Git commit and fork admission; settled ownership permits both without source replay
original.failingAssertion: dist line 121: assert.throws(() => process.kill(pid, 0), ESRCH) -> Missing expected exception (actual undefined)
original.notFailing: Both busy rejections (commit and fork admission while the host command owned the workspace) and closed.state === 'cancelled' with cleanupConfirmed === true passed before it.

hypotheses.check: Local PID allocation: 100 sequential spawns strictly increasing; 0/100 immediate reuse of a just-freed PID.

40 trials of a 200 MB child in its own group: after SIGTERM the (killpg, kill) states went live -> zombie (EPERM/ok) only; never ESRCH from killpg while kill(pid) succeeded. A zombie-only group returns EPERM (also from a non-parent process), which groupExists treats as present.
hypotheses.result: not supported; the engine's group check waits for reaping on macOS

hypotheses.check: The host script wrote the PID with writeFileSync while the test waited only for existsSync. writeFileSync creates the file before writing, so a loaded reader can see it empty; Number('') is 0 and process.kill(0, 0) signals the caller's own process group and succeeds without an exception.
hypotheses.result: consistent with the exact failure; not directly observed on the hosted runner

precedent: sandbox/boundaries.integration.test publishes held.pid with write-then-rename and asserts a positive safe integer; agent-backends crash-effects waits for /^[1-9]\d*$/ content.

resolution.change: The host script writes <pid>.tmp and renames it to the PID path; the test asserts the parsed PID is a positive safe integer before using it.
resolution.productConclusion: The engine's ownership fencing and cleanup confirmation behaved correctly in the failing attempt.

otherReaders: Other PID-file readers either publish atomically, validate the content, or read after the process has settled; none was changed.
